results.title: CBP Updates Section 232 Tariff Changes for Imports from Taiwan
results.content:
Retroactive impact: Entries since May 1, 2026, may require review and correction.
 Refund opportunities: Importers may file Post Summary Corrections (PSC) to recover overpaid duties.
 Drawback: Remains available for eligible duties.
 Additional duty exclusions: Certain qualifying Taiwanese automotive parts are not subject to overlapping Section 232 duties on aluminum, steel, copper (and derivative products), or specified wood product tariffs. [...] Key Highlights

Automobile Parts

 New Chapter 99 tariff provisions (HTSUS 9903.94.66- 9903.94.69) apply.
 Duty treatment depends on the base rate:
  + ≥15% base duty → no additional Section 232 duty
  + <15% base duty → 15% total combined duty
 A self-certification option is available for qualifying parts used in the U.S. automotive production or repair.

Wood Products

 Certain products are subject to an additional 15% duty under HTSUS 9903.76.24 [...] Create PDF

In Cargo Systems Messaging Service (CSMS) #68762890, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) issued new guidance implementing tariff-related provisions under a U.S. – Taiwan trade and security agreement. These updates modify the application of certain Section 232 duties on imports of automobile parts, wood products, and civil aircraft components.

The changes are effective retroactively for entries on or after May 1, 2026, and may impact recent filings.

results.title: ABPA Member Update: New U.S.-Taiwan Trade Agreement & the Effects on Auto Parts Imports – Automotive Body Parts Association (ABPA)
results.content:
What Changed for Auto Parts from Taiwan

Under the U.S.–Taiwan trade framework announced on January 15, tariffs on goods imported from Taiwan, including automotive parts, will be capped at no more than 15 percent. This includes any duties applied under Section 232, the national security authority that has previously been used to impose tariffs on auto parts. [...] For ABPA members, this is an important clarification. While tariffs are not being eliminated, the agreement provides a clear upper limit and avoids the risk of higher or more punitive duty rates that had been a concern in recent trade discussions. The tariff level brings Taiwan more in line with other major U.S. trading partners in the Asia-Pacific region and helps maintain Taiwan as a competitive and reliable source of automotive components.

Why Semiconductors Are Getting the Headlines [...] Much of the public attention around this announcement is centered on semiconductors, driven by large investment commitments by Taiwanese chip manufacturers and U.S. efforts to expand domestic semiconductor production. These provisions include incentives and tariff measures that are largely unrelated to automotive parts.

results.title: How Tariffs Are Affecting the PCB Circuit Board Industry
results.content: Printed circuit boards (PCBs) are the backbone of most technology on the planet. They power everything from smartphones and machine learning algorithms to microwaves and air fryers. While many of the tech companies that work with and rely on these PCBs are based in the United States, most of the PCBs themselves are manufactured overseas in countries like China, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea. Therefore, creating the next iPhone or the latest digital camera often means importing PCBs and [...] At present, there is a 10% universal tariff on most goods imported to the U.S. However, individual nations and specific goods have also been targeted with their own specific tariffs based on the status of their trade relationship. Japanese cars, for instance, face a 25% tariff. At the moment, there are no U.S. tariffs on printed circuit board imports specifically. However, imported PCBs and their components and materials are still subjected to both the universal 10% tariff and the tariffs [...] China — the largest producer of PCBs in the world — has been the primary target of the administration’s tariffs. As such, imported goods from China currently face the highest country-specific tariff rates of any nation in the world, with the average imported good facing a 30% tariff at the very least. However, even this lowered tariff rate may not last, as it is the result of a 90-day trade agreement between the U.S. and China.
